messages.subject: Simulate actionbutton action
parts:
Hi,

Is there a way to simulate the action done by an actionButton without clicking on it ?
For instance, imagine that i have an reactive function RF to an actionbutton "A".
I also have a reactive value <-reactiveValues (val =10).
I want to execute RF when clicking on "A" or when value$val>100, is there an easy way to do this.

To sum up, i want something like that: if value$>100 then "simulate click" on A.

Best,

messages.author: d6ebe55625e8e5a2
messages.subject: Re: Simulate actionbutton action
parts:
Can you elaborate on why you actually need to simulate an actionButton click? We explicitly never allow you to change the value of an actionButton because we don't think there's a legitimate use case for this and it promotes bad coding practices in Shiny. See this discussion for an idea of previous discussions and Joe's opinion. This is also why you can change a label of an actionButton (using updateActionButton()), but not its value.

So, in your use case, why not just trigger the same action based on those two different events (event A: when the actionButton input$A is clicked; and event B: when value$val > 100)? 

[Aside: as of the release of Shiny 1.0.1, we now have a new function called reactiveVal() that allows to create a singe reactive value, instead of requiring you to create a list of reactive values with reactiveValues().]

Here a minimal example, following your scenario:

library(shiny)

ui <- fluidPage(
  actionButton("A", "A"),
  numericInput("val", "Val", 10)
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  
  # this doesn't actually need to be reactive in this example
  RF <- function() {
    print("Either input$val > 100 OR input$A was clicked")
  }
  
  observeEvent(input$A, { RF() }, ignoreNULL = TRUE)
  observeEvent(req(input$val > 100), { RF() })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
